label: Site confounds creatinine (lab + enrolment)
text: PITFALL: SITE is documented as the hospital that enrolled the patient AND ran the blood tests, so site-level creatinine assay calibration differences (Jaffe vs enzymatic, IDMS traceability) combined with different statin prevalence per site can create or reverse a pooled statin-creatinine difference (Simpson's paradox). CHECK: tabulate statin prevalence and mean/median creatinine by SITE; compare the pooled statin effect with the within-site effects. IF FOUND: base the conclusion on a site-stratified or site-adjusted estimate (regression with SITE fixed effects, or stratified Mantel-Haenszel/van Elteren-type test), not the pooled comparison; report if direction differs. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1373/clinchem.2005.059659 (Myers et al., creatinine standardization); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simpson%27s_paradox (search tool unavailable; source not re-verified this session).

label: Reverse-coded radiotherapy flag
text: PITFALL: PRIOR_RADIOTHERAPY is reverse-coded in data_clinical_patient.txt (1 = not received, 0 = received), so a naive 1-vs-0 comparison flips the sign of the effect. CHECK: read the column description line and cross-tabulate PRIOR_RADIOTHERAPY against RT_DOSE_GY (received patients should have dose > 0, non-received dose = 0). IF FOUND: recode to received = (PRIOR_RADIOTHERAPY == 0) or use RT_DOSE_GY > 0 before comparing groups. SOURCE: data dictionary in the file header (web search unavailable).

label: Age/sex confounding of creatinine
text: PITFALL: Serum creatinine depends strongly on sex (men higher, muscle mass) and age, and statin users are typically older and more often male, so an unadjusted comparison can show statin users with HIGHER or lower creatinine purely through confounding. CHECK: compare AGE and SEX distributions between STATIN_USE groups; fit creatinine ~ STATIN_USE + AGE + SEX + SITE (optionally BMI from supplement). IF FOUND: use the adjusted coefficient for the verdict and state both crude and adjusted estimates. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1114248 (CKD-EPI creatinine equations use age/sex) (not re-verified this session).

label: Mixed lab units by site
text: PITFALL: some rows report labs in SI units (cholesterol around 4-6 mmol/L, calcium around 2.3 mmol/L, glucose around 4-6 mmol/L) while others use mg/dL (cholesterol 130-230). This appears tied to SITE C1, and mixing the two gives a massive artefactual group difference. CHECK: plot or summarise TOTAL_CHOLESTEROL, SERUM_CALCIUM and FASTING_GLUCOSE by SITE, and flag cholesterol < 20. IF FOUND: convert cholesterol mmol/L to mg/dL by multiplying by 38.67 (calcium x4.008, glucose x18.016), or analyse within site / exclude the SI site as a sensitivity check. Do not drop those values as outliers. SOURCE: standard SI conversion factors, e.g. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK83505/ (not retrieved; web search unavailable).

label: Unit mix / outliers in creatinine
text: PITFALL: Creatinine may be recorded in mixed units (mg/dL vs umol/L, factor 88.4) or contain implausible/sentinel values, especially if one site reports differently; such values dominate means. CHECK: per-SITE range of SERUM_CREATININE; flag values >20 (likely umol/L) or <=0, and missing codes. IF FOUND: convert umol/L to mg/dL (divide by 88.4) where clearly in that unit, else exclude, and rerun; prefer a robust/rank-based test as sensitivity. SOURCE: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK507821/ (StatPearls creatinine) (not re-verified this session).

label: Site confounding
text: PITFALL: site is likely to confound the comparison because both treatment proportion and lab method/units may differ by site, so a pooled difference can reverse or vanish within sites (Simpson's paradox). CHECK: cross-tabulate received radiotherapy by SITE and compute the cholesterol difference within each site after unit harmonisation. IF FOUND: report a site-stratified or site-adjusted estimate (regression with SITE as a fixed effect) as the primary result. SOURCE: general confounding guidance, e.g. https://www.bmj.com/content/349/bmj.g5557 (not retrieved).

label: Unit of analysis duplication
text: PITFALL: The sample table can have several samples per patient; joining it to the patient table before testing duplicates patient-level creatinine and statin values and inflates n / false significance. CHECK: count rows per PATIENT_ID in each table; check that the analysis unit is one row per patient. IF FOUND: analyse creatinine from data_clinical_patient.txt only (one row per patient); do not merge sample-level tables, which contain no relevant variables. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.316.7139.1236 (Altman & Bland, units of analysis) (not re-verified this session).

label: Direction and labelling of result
text: PITFALL: a direction-specific claim (received RT has LOWER cholesterol) can be wrongly labelled True from a pooled significant difference that runs the other way or comes only from the unit artefact. CHECK: after recoding and unit harmonisation, report the mean/median difference (received minus not received) with a 95% CI and a Welch t-test or Mann-Whitney test, overall and within site. IF FOUND: label True only if received is lower and the result is robust. If received is clearly higher, label False. A null result with clean variables is evidence against the claim, not 'Not verifiable', because the variables exist. SOURCE: general statistical practice (web search unavailable).

label: Skew and exposure coding
text: PITFALL: Creatinine is right-skewed and group sizes may be unequal, so a t-test on raw values can be driven by a few high (CKD) values; also STATIN_USE and STATIN_DOSE_MG may be inconsistent (e.g. use=0 with dose>0). CHECK: inspect distribution/skew per group; cross-tab STATIN_USE vs STATIN_DOSE_MG>0. IF FOUND: use Mann-Whitney or log-creatinine regression as primary/sensitivity; resolve or drop inconsistent exposure records and report; a dose-response trend within users is supportive evidence. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.312.7038.1079 (Bland & Altman, log transformation) (not re-verified this session).

label: Covariate adjustment
text: PITFALL: age, sex and BMI (BMI is in data_clinical_supplement.txt) affect cholesterol and may differ between RT groups, which biases a crude comparison. CHECK: compare AGE, SEX and BMI across RT groups, and fit cholesterol ~ RT + AGE + SEX + BMI + SITE after joining on PATIENT_ID. IF FOUND: report the adjusted estimate next to the crude one and note any change in sign. SOURCE: general confounding guidance (web search unavailable).

label: Label decision rule
text: PITFALL: Deciding the label: a non-significant or opposite-direction result is not automatically 'False'; 'False' requires evidence contradicting the claim (e.g. statin users significantly higher or a clearly null precise estimate), and 'Not verifiable' is only for missing variables - here STATIN_USE and SERUM_CREATININE exist, so Not verifiable is unlikely appropriate. CHECK: report adjusted effect size with 95% CI and its direction. IF FOUND: if crude and site/age/sex-adjusted results disagree, trust the adjusted one and explain. SOURCE: https://doi.org/10.1007/s10654-016-0149-3 (Greenland et al., misinterpretation of P values) (not re-verified this session).

label: Patient vs sample level
text: PITFALL: data_clinical_sample.txt has one row per sample, so joining it to patient-level data can duplicate patients and inflate n. The sample table is not needed for a patient-level cholesterol question. CHECK: confirm that PATIENT_ID is unique in the patient table and count rows after any merge. IF FOUND: analyse at patient level, using one row per patient. SOURCE: cBioPortal clinical file format docs https://docs.cbioportal.org/file-formats/ (not retrieved).
